case.initial_facts:
This is an autopsy-tissue series, not an individual diagnostic vignette. Eight deceased people with SOD1-associated ALS had received intrathecal tofersen. Tissue concentrations were examined against dosing histories and pharmacokinetic predictions.
In three recently treated donors, lumbar spinal-cord SOD1 mRNA/protein reductions were reported in the range 45%–84%, relative to tofersen-naive tissue samples. The size and matching of that comparison cohort are not specified in this packet. Residual motor neurons contained drug-related signal; misfolded SOD1 inclusions remained detectable. This packet supplies no randomised clinical comparison, patient-level functional trajectory or survival estimate.

case.hidden: The paper also describes meningeal/perivascular infiltrates and other mechanistic findings. They are not supplied here and are not required. Other clinical trials discussed in the source are outside this packet.
case.reference: The eight-donor study and three-donor reduction subset must remain distinct. Tissue distribution and reduced target measures support biological target engagement in sampled tissue. They do not by themselves estimate clinical benefit, comparative survival, universal response or an individual treatment recommendation. The 45%–84% range is not a clinical response rate or an effect in all eight donors. Lack of a supplied functional comparison should be acknowledged without dismissing the measured tissue results.
